correctness.rationale: For every jointly susceptible vertex, the local pair-outcome rule is necessary and sufficient by separating common, unvaccinated-only and vaccinated-only infective sources. Different targets use disjoint directed-edge contacts. The checker enumerates the entire reachable 140-state closure from seed/vaccination under all shared contact choices for n=5; no adverse terminal state exists. Smaller graphs embed via absent contacts and isolated vertices. A six-vertex contact history has different infection arrival times and exact target risks 0 and 1; multilinearity of finite-horizon probabilities proves an open set of strict adverse risks. All hypotheses and boundaries are stated in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The fully read Floyd–Kay–Shapiro 2007 preprint proves vaccination monotonicity with fixed-time transmission probabilities and discusses that temporally varying probabilities can cause collateral harm. The present statement instead determines the exact sharp number of people needed for the temporally varying failure; no such threshold is in the accessible preprint or recovered closest research records. Novelty remains a qualified best-knowledge judgment, not a claim that no unindexed earlier result exists.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier combinatorial SIR finite-network results could implicitly give the same sharp six-person cutoff.
Other longer-period or multiple-seed epidemic models are outside scope; no implication claimed for them.
Independent mathematical review and literature review have not yet been performed.

value.rationale: The sharp minimal population size for collateral infection is a natural, model-intrinsic boundary of the classical vaccination monotonicity paradox. Five-person pathwise immunity holds even under arbitrary calendar-time contact changes, yet an explicit six-person motif defeats it. This resolves a meaningful finite network threshold beyond a mere isolated numerical counterexample, without claiming general real-world vaccine harms.
